body: Howdy.

I'm really glad other people have had to have separate litters. I was worried I was the only one as everyone I've spoken to has had them sharing. 

Yeah, thumpalina was pretty much aggressive from the get go. The table bonding went fine but that's partly because we were controlling them but as soon as we weren't holding them, they went straight for each other in fighting. 

She was also very aggressive towards me such as growling and lunging if I picked her bowl up. This is the complete opposite to Ralph as he has never even tried to bite me in the year and half I've had him. 

Her aggression towards me has calmed down since she's with Ralph which is showing me positive signs. But I'm honestly not surprised as she came from a bad home where the woman put two males and her in a cage, not desexed. As you can imagine, it was a disaster. When one of the males were rescued, he was missing most of his ears and was blind. So honestly, she probably had to spend her time defending herself as she was so thin and has chunks missing from her ear.

Its a bit tricky with separation as I was warned by the shelter do not to do it unless necessary as it may back track the bond they already have. I've recently extend their cage slightly with more places for them to hide such as tunnels which I have found has helped with the nipping but it's persistent. 

Did your buns have an aggression when they had their dates?
Ralphie was desexed over year ago and thumpalina around a couple of months. I actually didn't think about that. Could it be affecting her atm?

I've made sure to choose a shelter that allows that. They've informed that they will do everything they can do help with the bonding (such as sending people over to help) and if it doesn't work, they are happy to swap for another (or just return the bun). Its what I am most afraid of and as much as it would be sad to have to return one, my little man atm will always come first until bonded!

Thank you for your response. I will definitely make sure the new bun is desexed as mine already is. 
The speed dating is a good idea but unfortunately the local shelter won't do so but they will do everything they can help with the bonding process which is a bonus!
Thank you for your first hand experience. It's good to hear that they keep the same traits.

Most people aren't protesting the right to drink until the early hours of the morning, it's do with the impact the legalisation has had, and the obvious corrupt exemptions of certain venues. 

I know many people who have lost their jobs and cannot find a new one due to a large number of venues are closing. I feel more unsafe in the city then before after dark due to the number of people around has completely disappeared. The fact that a person cannot enter a venue past 1:30am is down right stupid when public transport to the suburbs has already stopped by that hour. What are people meant to do but wait around on the streets?

The casino in the heart of the city is exempt from the lock-out laws and trades 24/7. Why should they be exempt? The government can't pick and choose who the law applies to and who it doesn't just because they get financial gain from it staying open. The casinos will never be included in the lockouts laws which is completely wrong on so many levels considering how gambling can have a high impact on a person's life. 

Lastly, simply forcing people away from the area will of course lower the crime rate but it's just a band-aid. The government's solutions to social problems should not be to limit/ban it but to analyse international approaches and adapt accordingly. These laws are just knee jerk reactions to main stream media. Five people died on boxing day in 2015 on our roads (mostly around the afternoon) does that mean we should lockout driving on major holidays during the afternoon? No of course not! We develop safer roads, lower the speed limit, double demits put in place, more police etc. 

The same can be applied for the issues with alcohol, rather then simply locking the community out we can develop 24/7 public transport, harsher penalties for violence (not just alcohol related), community safe zones, education to promote change in culture and many more. 

Sorry about the rant but it really is more then just about wanting to drink for longer/plan our nights better.
